issues.legal_issue: A substantial deduction from the value indicated by sales of small plots is justified when assessing compensation for a large tract with relevant locational and development constraints.
material_facts: A large tract of 7 acres and 28 gunthas was acquired for an orphanage.
The High Court assessed the land at Rs. 10 per square yard by reference to nearby sales, then deducted 60% and fixed compensation at Rs. 4 per square yard.
The comparable sales concerned small plots, whereas the acquired land was a large tract situated far from municipal limits.
Restrictions on development could be imposed, and land intended for building use would require provision of roads and other civic amenities.
The claimant owners had bought the tract in 1956 at Rs. 251 per acre, and neighbouring land was sold in 1960 at Rs. 960 per acre.
issues.conclusion: The 60% deduction was justified on the facts, and the Court declined to interfere with the compensation fixed by the High Court.
issues.legal_principle: Market value is determined by evaluating all relevant circumstances from the standpoint of a prudent willing purchaser, rather than by speculation. Under the principles discussed in Chimanlal Hargovinddas v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, Poona, relevant circumstances must be assessed on the evidence in each case. Administrator General of West Bengal v. Collector, Varanasi holds that the value of small developed plots is not directly a safe guide for a large tract, unless the tract is ripe for building use and a hypothetical layout is appropriate; deductions for roads and civic amenities may then be required. Bhagwathula Samana v. Special Tehsildar was distinguished because the land there was already in a developed area. The Court also considered the possibility of development restrictions under Section 74 of the Highways Act. The case arose from a compensation determination under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, including its Sections 4(1) and 54, challenged by appeal under Article 136 of the Constitution.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and large_acquired_tract and small_plot_comparables and (remote_from_municipal_limits or development_restrictions_possible)

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: A party appeals a determination of compensation for land acquired by the state.
predicates.large_acquired_tract: The acquired land is a large tract rather than a small individual plot.
predicates.small_plot_comparables: The valuation relies on sales of plots substantially smaller than the acquired tract.
predicates.remote_from_municipal_limits: The acquired land is situated far from municipal limits.
predicates.development_restrictions_possible: Restrictions on developing the acquired land may be imposed.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal concerns a large acquired tract valued by reference to small plots, and the tract is remote from municipal limits or may face development restrictions, the rule upholds a substantial deduction in market value.
